Short answer: for 2024, generally no — unreimbursed employee business expenses (including a home‑office used solely as a W‑2 employee) are not deductible because the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act suspended miscellaneous itemized deductions subject to the 2% floor for tax years 2018–2025.

If a home‑office deduction were available (for example, for a self‑employed taxpayer), you must substantiate exclusive/regular use, square footage and allocation methods, direct vs. indirect expenses, receipts and contemporaneous records, and employer statements about workspace requirements or reimbursements. 

There are very narrow statutory exceptions that have historically allowed some employees (e.g., certain reservists, some performing artists or fee‑basis officials) to deduct business expenses under separate provisions, but those exceptions are uncommon and governed by their own code sections and rules. 

Conservatively speaking, unless one of those rare statutory exceptions applies or you are self‑employed, your documented home‑office costs as a W‑2 employee will not produce a federal deduction on your 2024 return.
